title: DayEntry
description: The runner's daily feedback — the input the whole product depends on. Design constraint: tier 1 (outcome, RPE, legs) is enough to generate a comment and a micro-adjustment, so the minimum viable save is 3 taps. Everything deeper is optional and progressively disclosed. Corrections never overwrite: they create a new revision with superseded_by (AGENTS.md rule 4). Two axes, named apart since 2026-11-04 (docs/engineering/contract-vocabulary.md item 20): `outcome` is what happened to the day, `sessionTaken` is what was actually done against the prescription. One field used to hold both, and it could not hold the runner's answers at all: five of its seven values were unstorable.

userId.description: Server-assigned from session; ignored if sent by the client (RLS is the enforcement, not this field).

day.description: Training day per calendar-and-time.md#1, i.e. the day whose 04:00 boundary contains the activity — not the calendar date of the timestamp.

correctionReason.description: Required when correcting a day older than 72 h (feedback-loop.md backfill rule).

tzAtEvent.description: IANA zone at the time of the activity; makes travel honest.

idempotencyKey.description: Offline-safe resubmission; unique per (userId, day, revision).

outcome.description: What happened to the day. The same five values the column stores (day_entries.outcome), because a runner's answer that no column can hold is not a feature. `rest` is a day accounted for, not a hole; `partial` is meaningful work below the prescription and is the input the next micro-adjust reads; `skipped` is the runner's own report; `missed` is the system's verdict on a day that closed with no entry, written at the day-start rollup and never submitted by a runner (formerly spelled `unlogged`). `completed` means the session was done in full - whether as prescribed, as the planned alternate, or beyond it is the next field's business.

sessionTaken.description: What was actually done, relative to the prescription. `alternate` is a success - the planned alternate was chosen - and counts toward load but never toward running ramp maths; `extra` is more than prescribed and subtracts rather than earning credit (missed-session-rules.yaml#extra-activity-subtracts); `partial` is part of the prescription, and it requires the outcome `partial` plus a completedKm or durationMin, because a part with no amount is not a fact; `none` is nothing. When the runner did not say, the key is ABSENT - null is not a value this contract accepts, and the description used to say otherwise. Deliberately not folded into `outcome`: the same outcome can be a different session, and the rules need both facts separately.

outcomeDetail.description: One tap. Highest-value/lowest-cost field in the product: intent changes the decision more than the miss itself (missed-session-rules.yaml). Formerly `statusDetail`, which named a field that no longer exists. Stored in day_entries.outcome_detail, which is why the reasons are storable at all - before 2026-11-04 they had no column.

completedKm.description: If omitted, the planner uses distanceKm from the linked activity, then prescribed distance with lower confidence.

rpe.description: Session RPE, Borg CR10. Drives load_sRPE and the rpe_gap signal. Not the same as 'legs'.

legs.description: 1 feathered · 2 normal · 3 heavy · 4 very heavy · 5 wrecked. The most plan-relevant single subjective item for runners.

mood.description: Displayed, and used only as a weak tiebreaker. Never used to judge or to nudge (feedback-microcopy.md#never-say).

wellness.description: Tier 2. Collapsed in the UI and remembers yesterday's value.

hrvLnRMSSD.description: ln-transformed; the metric contract expects natural-log RMSSD (metric-definitions.md#hrv_lnrmssd_dev).

muscleSoreness.description: Tier 2 muscle soreness, 1-5. Canonical spelling since 2026-11-04 (docs/roadmap/backlog.md row 17); this is the name every decision reads.

musoreSoreness.description: Deprecated misspelling of `muscleSoreness`, accepted only for a migration window that ends 2027-02-04. A write that carries it is normalised to `muscleSoreness` before storage, and a write that carries both is refused; new clients must send the canonical name.

illnessSymptoms.description: Drives the safety layer: 'below-neck' or 'fever' is a hard stop, non-overridable (safety-layer.md#1).

fuelingNote.description: Free text only. We never respond with calorie or weight guidance; long-run fueling guidance is generic and product-agnostic.

pain.description: Body-map or text. The triage input for injury-risk-and-pain-triage.md; drives constrain/advise/hard_stop.

site.description: Controlled body-part code preferred; free text allowed and normalised.

nextMorningWorse.description: The single most useful pain question we ask.

affectsGait.description: true => immediate constrain at minimum; night pain or gait change escalates.

note.description: Sent to the narrator only as intent codes unless aiNarratorEnabled and minimisation rules pass (ADR-0006).

intent.description: 'just-check-me' produces a read-only verdict with no action; the highest-signal reason a runner opens the app.

source.description: How it was captured. 'offline-queue' entries replay with their original idempotency key.

linkedActivityIds.description: Set by the identity matcher or the runner, never assumed: autoLinked requires confidence above threshold, else 'suggested' (integrations.md#import-pipeline).
